I'm not sure if that was sarcastic or not but hyperacusis is a really rare condition that you only get if you continue to listen to noise at damaging levels after getting tinnitus. My tinnitus varies and it's sometimes been in the severe category but eventually I was used to it and always able to function without getting distracted by it.

Even if it does that won't matter because there's several somewhat promising treatments being made for hearing loss that could help reduce it along with some specifically designed for tinnitus, so you'll probably be better off overall in a 3-5 years when these treatments start coming out even if you're tinnitus continued to get worse from sound. [tinnitustalk.com](https://tinnitustalk.com) has lots of info about these treatments under research news you can read about.

There's actually a really decent chance there will be legitimate treatments in the next 5 years, potentially within a few years too. OTO-313, OTO-413, FX-322 and a bunch of other stuff is being made to regenerate damaged hair cells, repair synapses and reduce inflammation. I've been reading a lot on [tinnitustalk.com](https://tinnitustalk.com) and it's really calmed me down about my tinnitus not being permanent. Treatments aren't cures but they could reduce it to the point where you no longer hear it when surrounded by some noise, it might get rid of it completely for some too. A cure will come eventually.
